name: Suspension Hip Press
definition: A bilateral supine suspension-trainer bridge with both heels in the foot cradles and both knees held bent. Hip extension raises the pelvis to a controlled neutral endpoint before a controlled return; the knees do not curl and extend to create the repetition. The fixture is rep-tracked and non-comparable because strap length, body position, and technique change the effective load. Suspension hamstring curls, straight-leg hip lifts, single-leg bridges, floor bridges, and externally loaded hip thrusts remain outside this family.

variantAxes.description: The upper body remains floor supported.
Both heels are carried by the suspension trainer.
The knees stay bent instead of curling through the repetition.
The hips create the bridge repetition.
The straps do not constrain the body to a machine path.

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your back with both heels in the foot cradles, both knees bent, arms on the floor, and the straps set around mid-calf height.
execution.movement: Press through both heels and extend the hips to lift the pelvis while holding the knee angles steady.
execution.endpoint: Stop when the hips reach neutral and the trunk and thighs form a straight line without the low back arching.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the pelvis under control while keeping both knees bent and both heels in the cradles.
execution.controlledJoints: Create the repetition at the hips; do not curl or straighten the knees to move the body.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the head, shoulders, and arms supported, the pelvis level, and pressure even through both heels.
disqualifyingCompensations: Bending and straightening the knees turns the repetition into a hamstring curl.
Overarching the low back instead of extending the hips leaves the reviewed bridge.
Using one leg changes the two-leg fixture.
